rubrics.justification: Generally consistent with the provided 3AA label, but the image itself does not clearly show a well-expanded blastocoel occupying most of the embryo, nor clear TE detail; mention of early herniation is speculative.

Integrates age, ovarian reserve, male factor, prior biochemical pregnancy, smoking, endometrium, and stimulation context with embryo quality, though some links are overstated or not strongly evidence-based.

Overall structured and logical, but several conclusions rely on speculative penalties and assumptions (e.g., thick endometrium impact, smoking effect magnitude, biochemical pregnancy implying aneuploidy risk).

Appropriate support for single embryo transfer and trigger review, but recommendations such as routine low-dose aspirin, ERA after one failure, and broad PGT-A endorsement at age 35 are not strongly guideline-based.
Provides clear next-step recommendations for transfer, lifestyle modification, and future stimulation review, though some suggested interventions are more opinion-based than standard practice.
